The magnetic field of the solution belongs locally to the Sobolev space HI and depends smoothly on frequencies and incident angles of the incoming plane wave with exception of the Rayleigh frequencies. These properties allow to use standard 3D finite elements to solve the boundary value problem

articleTitle: Asymptotical Analysis of Electrostatic Problems in Nonlinear Domains with Thin Perfectly Conducting Grids
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In the paper we investigate the asymptotic behavior of solutions of the family of nonlinear elliptic equations in domains with thin grids concentrating near a hypersurface when the measure of wires tends to zero and the density tends to infinity. The homogenized equations and the homogenized boundary conditions are derived. The homogenization technique is based on the applying of the abstract theorem on the homogenization of the nonlinear variational functional in the Sobolev-Orlicz spaces. This theorem is proved in the paper

articleTitle: Quasi-Intermittency Ofwaves and their Complexity in Modulated Dielectric Medium
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A correlation between the Hurst's index of an electromagnetic signal and its complexity in time-varying medium is shown

articleTitle: Modal Study of "Tweek"-Atmospherics
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A new technique is used for analysis polarization parameters of experimental records of tweek-atmospherics (tweeks). Tweeks are observed during nighttime and represent a response of the Earth-ionosphere waveguide excited by lightning strokes. Tweeks are formed by series of pulses consecutively reflected from the waveguide boundaries under different incident angles depending on a source-observer distance and average effective ionosphere height along a propagation path. Using a source location technique described in our previous works we determined geometrical propagation path parameters such as source range, ionosphere height, and orientation of a propagation path in refer to magnetic meridian. We used then a time-frequency representation of the analyzed tweek waveforms to infer polarization parameters of the electromagnetic waves propagated under different incident angles as the first waveguide mode. Obtained dependencies of these polarization parameters show substantial difference depending on a propagation path length and its orientation

articleTitle: Periodic layered media without stop bands
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The one-dimensional periodic media containing usual isotropic, backward wave, bianisotropic (anisotropic) are studied in this paper. The kinds of periodic structures that have no stop bands are found. The rigorous analytical proof and physical description of this phenomenon is given.

articleTitle: Angular Spectrum Representation in Nonparaxial Propagation
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Properties of the boundary field Fourier spectrum in the angular spectrum representation are considered. It is shown that the spectrum has singularities at points which separate spatial frequencies of propagating and evanescent modes. Therefore functions with continuous spectrum are physically impossible and can be used for simulations only with analysis of approximation errors

articleTitle: Synthetic Conformal Mappings for Analysis of Complex 2-D and 3-D Conductor Arrangements
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The closed-form conformal mappings for auxiliary canonical domains have been adapted to obtain the equivalent circuit parameters of two- (2-D) and three-dimensional (3-D) conductor arrangements of complex shapes. Combined with the distributed circuit analysis, the developed synthetic models enable for the solution of both a direct problem of analysis and an inverse problem of retrieving physical dimensions from the specified electrical parameters. Enhanced algorithms for evaluating elliptic functions and elliptic integrals (EI) of the 1st kind were devised to overcome the crowding effect and provide rapidly convergent solutions for a broad range of the structure dimensions. Applications of the developed approach will be illustrated by the examples of rectangular coaxial lines, coupled bars, step discontinuities, chip capacitors, resonators, etc

articleTitle: Waves of Electromagnetic Field Correlations in Hydrodynamic Plasma
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Closed system of equations for binary correlations of electromagnetic field and hydrodynamic medium (many component plasma) has been obtained and linearized near equilibrium. Ideal gas approximation was studied. Coupled hydrodynamic and transversal plasma waves for correlations of electromagnetic field was predicted

articleTitle: Green's functions and integral equations for photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The scalar and tensor (dyadic) Green's functions (GFs) for three-dimensional-periodic (3DP), two-dimensional- periodic (2DP) and one-dimensional-periodic (1DP) sources have been considered and corresponding volume, surface and coupled volume-surface integral equations (IEs) and integrodifferential equations (IDEs) have been derived. The 3DP, 2DP, and 1DP IEs have been used to simulate the photonic crystal (PC) structures with periodic dielectric body and metallic wire inclusions. The homogenization and photonic bandgap (PBG) structures in the lossy PCs have been considered and investigated

articleTitle: Geometrical Editor for Electromagnetic Simulation System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: New geometrical editor for electromagnetic solver MWD02 is presented. It combines an intuitive GUI based on the AutoCAD working environment and a simple way for analyzing the circuits, creating new library elements and performing a wide range of every-day microwave engineering tasks

articleTitle: The Analysis and Matching of Finline with "Open Diode" in Slot
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: This paper proposes an electrodynamics model of an open pin-diode placed in a finline. An accurate hybrid-mode analysis is presented to determine the normalized propagation constants of a unilateral finline and finline with metal-dielectric insertion. This insertion simulates the behavior of open diode in finline. The algorithms of calculation of the modal-S-matrix on the step and metal-dielectric insertion discontinuities are developed. Based on data describing losses in open diode, the matching circuits for microwave attenuator were designed based on the finline alternating quarter-wave-length sections

articleTitle: The Internal Admittance of Slot in a Waveguide with a Dielectric Slab of Finite Length
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A narrow slot situated above a dielectric slab of finite length, fully filling the cross section of a rectangular waveguide is considered. Magnetic field excited by this slot under it in the slab is found. The inner admittance of the slot and its energetic parameters are numerically studied

articleTitle: On Spherical Wavec Scattering by an Electrically Small Layered Sphere and a Related Inverse Problem
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A spherical electromagnetic wave is scattered by a layered sphere with a perfect electric conducting core. Low frequency results are obtained by approximating the known exact expressions of the scattering cross section. The inverse problem of determining the sphere's center and the layers radii and materials is treated from the knowledge of the leading order term of the scattering cross section's low-frequency expansion

articleTitle: Verification and Simulation Error Estimation for the Model of Electromagnetic Field Distribution in the Human Head Phantom
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A mathematical model of electromagnetic field distribution in the human head phantom is elaborated. In simulations, the integral equation method is applied. Experimental verification of the designed models and simulation error estimation are discussed. The modeling results are compared with other authors results obtained by the FDTD method

articleTitle: Meteorological Object Characteristics Estimation with Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: An example of network application for Doppler echo-signal processing is shown. The structure of neural network for such kind of operation is studied. A classical method and neural method in the calculation of eddy dissipation rate are considered and a comparison of results is done

articleTitle: Null-Field Method Enhancement Technique for the Investigation of Scattering from Inclusions in Plane-Layered Media
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In the present report, within the framework of a null-field method (NFM), new approach of a renormalization of the system of linear algebraic equations concerning coefficients of expansion of the unknown field on the contour of the scatterer is proposed. The effect of the proposed approach on the efficiency of computer algorithm in the solution of the problems of diffraction of electromagnetic waves on inclusions in plane layered media is discussed. Some results of numerical calculations are given

articleTitle: Computational Model of the Doppler Spectrum of Radar Returns from Rain
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: This paper presents the computational model of Doppler spectrum that considers the influence of the shape of turbulence spectrum onto the spectrum of echo-signal from rain at different intensity of turbulence and rain rate. The inertia of raindrops is taken into account. The developed approach allows calculating Doppler spectrum at different conditions. Validation with real data is done

articleTitle: Attenuation of the Earth Wave on the Fractal Radiopath
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A ground wave of the Earth electromagnetic field is considered. Characteristics of the module of an attenuation function for an inhomogeneous fractal radiopath are considered, with a Cantor set that describes distribution of electric parameters sigma and epsiv on the Earth surface is used. Electric parameters are modeled with equivalent electric circuits

articleTitle: Analysis of Composite Textiles Filled with Arbitrarily Oriented Conducting Fibres Using a Periodic Model for Crossed Strips
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Composite textiles formed by regular fibres in combination with conducting fibres are analysed by using a model for a periodic array of crossed strips. Through comparison with measurements it is demonstrated that this simple model can provide a good first estimation of the shielding effectiveness for this kind of innovating materials

articleTitle: Light Scattering with Heterogeneous Core - Cladding Boundary in Dielectric Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Light scattering in dielectric waveguide is caused, inter alia by random heterogeneity of boundary separating core and cladding layers. Rigorous mathematical approach to the problem consists in solving Maxwell equations with stochastic boundary conditions, what seems to be inconvenient in practice. The reasonable alternative is to treat the heterogeneous boundary as perturbation of the refractive index in the thin boundary layer. In this case the vector wave equation reduces to the equations for random amplitudes of coupled modes, where the coupling depends on spatial correlations of the refractive index. In this paper we establish the analytic connection between the models of the heterogeneous boundary surface and the perturbed refractive index. We express the refractive index correlations in terms of the surface correlations. We investigate the coupling of orthogonally polarized modes and estimate scattering in planar optical waveguide

articleTitle: Radar Cross Section of Multielement Linear Dipole Arrays
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The radar cross section (RCS) of linear dipole array versus dipole number and observation point angle is analyzed. In the work the combination of two methods: the method analysis of complex objects RCS and method of integral equation (IE), are used

articleTitle: The development of a new calculation scheme for electromagnetic eigenwaves in 2D two-component systems in the 4-wave approach
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The new scheme of wave phenomena calculation in 2D two-component periodical systems was developed. The four-wave approach used in the scheme allows increase the computational power comparatively with existing finite difference method due to the bigger scale of phenomena which are included by the solution on each step of the procedure

articleTitle: Design of Filters Based on Photonic Crystal Slabs
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: To realize Photonic Crystal (PhC) slab based filters in integrated circuits, two methods using Perfect Electric Conductor (PEC) walls to replace periodic boundary conditions of the PhC slab and embedding a PhC filter in a conventional waveguide structure are presented. In the former case - as conductors at optical frequencies aren't PECs at all - a real metal (silver) was partially coated near the PhC holes along the sides of the trench waveguide to realize a PhC slab based filter. Although the coatings completely spoil the filter properties and the loss in metal reduces the filter quality (transmission, bandwidth, etc.), it is possible to reestablish the desired filter characteristics by using an optimization procedure that also takes the coating into account.

articleTitle: Degeneration of Solutions of the Floquet Problem for Electromagnetic Waves in the Spatially Periodic Medium
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: As to propagation and diffraction of waves in the periodic structures, the degeneration of solutions of the Floquet problem for the Meissner model has been determined for the first time. For a number of reflection regions the characteristic equations have been obtained

articleTitle: An Overview of Simple Localized Solutions of the Wave Equation
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: An overview of simple localized solutions of the wave equation is presented, focused on exact solutions. We consider Bateman-type solutions, which show a Gaussian localization, localized at infinity Moses-Prosser "acoustic and electromagnetic bullets" and their time-harmonic counterparts, "X-waves", etc. Paraxial beams, including Bessel-Gauss beams, are discussed in the framework of the parabolic-equation formalism. Methods of constructing both exact and paraxial approximate solutions are described

articleTitle: Analysis of an Arbitrary Profile Reflector Antenna System Having Resistive Type Surface - E-Polarization Case
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The regularized solution is performed for arbitrary shape conic section profile geometry. In this case the reflector surface is taken as made up of resistive type material. The problem is formulated depending on the circular 2pi periodicity and then Fourier series coefficients of the surface current density are obtained. The resultant matrix equation is in the regularized form. Then the various numerical results are obtained for different eccentricity factor of the conic section and the resistivity of the reflector surface

articleTitle: Photonic band-gaps in periodic lattices arrays
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We demonstrate that periodic lattice arrays can be formed by interferometry patterns. An advantage of this system is the possibility of change different geometries of periodic lattice arrays only varying the mirror of the experimental setup. The patterns can be recorded in a special film emulsion and we studied the photonic band-gaps for different geometries

articleTitle: Parameters extraction from inhomogeneous metamaterials with model based parameter estimation
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Numerical extraction of effective material parameters of metamaterials is limited by data noise that may be caused by inaccurate field solvers as well as by inaccurate measurements. In some areas, the extraction formulas strongly amplify the noise, which results in useless results. This paper demonstrates that these noise-related problems may be overcome when the model based parameter estimation technique is used for fitting the frequency dependence of S parameters.

articleTitle: Time-domain finite element modeling of weak acousto-optic interaction
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The time domain finite element modeling were applied to the Bragg acousto-optic cell, that allows for the analysis of impulse signals propagation. The weak acousto-optic interaction was investigated. Special attention was given to linearity subject

articleTitle: Axially-Symmetrical Radiators of Pulsed Tm0n-and Te0n-Waves
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The paper presents novel results associated with the simulation and analysis of axially-symmetrical radiators of pulsed waves

articleTitle: Integrated Photonic Crystal Devices for Optical Interconnect Applications (invited paper)
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The amount of information that can be handled by computers is increasing every year. In order to satisfy this growing demand, computers need to augment the number of components in a chip and, at the same time, operate at higher speeds. This is leading long electrical interconnects to reach their limits in terms of speed and power dissipation, motivating the search of new alternatives. One of the alternatives is to use optical interconnects, because they can operate at very high speeds, dissipate less power and are more immune to electrical interference. On the other hand, optical circuits in these optical interconnect systems cannot be much larger than their electronic counterparts, what opens an opportunity for photonic crystal circuits, due to their great potential to reduce dimensions in integrated optical circuits technology. In this presentation, we analyze a few photonic crystal devices which target optical interconnect applications

articleTitle: Rigorous Mathematical Model and Simulation for TM Waves in Coaxial Cavity Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: For the first time rigorous mathematical model is developed for TM modes in a coaxial cavity gyrotron. This theory has no restrictions and can be applied for any corrugation parameters and mode numbers. Simulation software has been developed to find eigen cut-off wave numbers and calculate electromagnetic field components for TM modes. Novel results of the simulations are presented for the ITER relevant 170GHz coaxial cavity gyrotron with the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">34,19</sub> operating mode

articleTitle: The light amplification effect in the scattering of a quasi-classical electron by a nucleus in the electromagnetic field
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: This paper is devoted to the amplification effect of an electromagnetic radiation in the electron scattering by ions in external electromagnetic field in the quasi-classical approximation. The light amplification effect was studied for the nonrelativistic quasi-classical electrons. All cases of possible amplification of an electromagnetic radiation are observed. Estimations of the gain coefficient in the radio frequencies region are done. Practical importance of the given effect is shown

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Characteristics of the Vertical Dipole Located Above a Metal Infinite Plane with a Ledge
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: On the basis of a method of the uniform geometrical theory of diffraction the far field of a vertical half-wave electric dipole located arbitrarily above a metal plane with a rectangular thin ledge is determined in all space of observation. The directive patterns of the orthogonal components of the vector of electric field intensity, radiation resistance, the directive gains of the dipole and factor of protective action of a ledge in the direction of normal to it were calculated versus the position of the dipole, as well as the ledge and the plane parameters

articleTitle: Implementation of adaptive multiscale moment method in analyzing a wide band E-shaped patch antenna for wireless communications
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper we employ adaptive multiscale moment method (AMMM) for the analyzing a wide band E-shaped patch antenna. This algorithm employs the conventional moment method and a special matrix transformation. The compression is applied directly to the solution then the size of the linear equations to be solved is reduced, thereby improving the efficiency of the conventional moment method. We were interested to implement this method in a 30.3% bandwidth E-shaped patch antenna, resonating at wireless communication frequencies of 1.9 and 2.4 GHz. The basic difference between this methodology and the other techniques presented so far is that we apply the compression not to the impedance matrix, but to the solution itself directly using an iterative solution methodology

articleTitle: Time-Domain Scattering from Arbitrary Array of Parallel Electric Dipoles
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Time-domain integro-differential equation with a logarithmic kernel is derived for the surface current density for an array of parallel electric dipoles. Equation regularization is made by the analytical transformation of the extracted singular static part. Numerical solution of the transformed equation with a smooth kernel is obtained by the collocation method. Time dependence of the current is approximated by the splines of the first kind

articleTitle: The Method of Early Fault Identification in a Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The method of early identification of the nonoperating wind electricity devices is suggested here. The main idea of this method consists in the assumption that the detection of a nonoperation is reflected by the detection of a periodic signal hidden in the noises with a long duration: practically its duration is longer than the duration of a measured succession and that is why one may consider this signal to be periodic with the constant amplitude and frequency. The principal work of the suggested system of early identification of the nonoperating devices consists in the usage of an operated Duffing oscillator. A small periodic signal hidden in the noise may be detected by Duffing oscillator, as a transition from the oscillation regime with a small amplitude to the regime with a high amplitude. Oscillator works as a highly sensitive frequency relay. For instance, the bearings damages have periodic character that is why the process of nonoperation may identify the detection of a periodic determined frequency signal in the informational signals. Vibroaccelerometers signals are used in the work, which are taken from the real equipments. Harmonic signal of a fixed frequency with different amplitude is used for nonoperation modeling to each of these signals. The aim of the research is to fix harmonic signal using at the correlation signal/noise smaller than 1. The results have shown the possible usage of the suggested method for the construction system of early debugging of nonoperating wind electricity aggregates at the signal-to-noise merit greater than -23 dB

articleTitle: Resonant response of metallic compound gratings with subwavelength slits
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We investigate the response of gratings formed by subwavelength wires and slits in a dielectric medium. Transmission metallic gratings with subwavelength slits are known to produce enhanced transmitted intensity for certain resonant wavelengths. One of the mechanisms that produce these resonances is the excitation of waveguide modes inside the slits. We show that when the period of the structure is formed by several wires and slits (compound grating), new degrees of freedom are introduced for the phase distribution of the field inside the slits, allowing a new class of resonances. Phase resonances appear as sharp features in the transmitted/reflected response and are characterized by a significant enhancement of the interior field. We investigate the response of such systems under normal and oblique illumination and show that new phase modes appear in this last case. Contrary to the effect produced by a defect in a photonic crystal, these systems exhibit forbidden channels within a permitted band. We also found that the appearance of these resonances is not highly dependent on the slits width and thickness, even though these parameters modify the overall transmittance. We give numerical examples illustrating the effect produced by these resonances in the grating response

articleTitle: Implementation of Various Array Geometreis in Smart Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Space division multiple access (SDMA) is a promising candidate for improving channel capacity in future wireless communication systems. Since the discrimination performance of the user in the spatial domain depends on the array arrangement, an optimum element arrangement for SDMA should be defined. The pattern of antenna array is determined by array geometry. Two-dimensional spatial filters that can be implemented by microstrip technology are capable of filtering the received signal in the angular domain as well as the frequency domain. This paper focuses on various geometry of eight and nine elements antenna array using circularly patch elements

articleTitle: The Over-Determined Boundary Value Problem Method for the Problems of Electromagnetic Waves Diffraction in the Waveguides with Metallic Bounds
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The auxiliary over-determined problems for the Maxwell equations set in the semi-infinity cylindrical domains with Cauchy conditions on the face are considered. The integral identities connecting the traces of the solutions on the face are obtained in the case of arbitrary cross-section of the domain. These identities are used to design the regularization method for integral equations of the diffraction problem on the different inhomogeneities in the waveguides with metallic sides. The over-determined boundary value problem for semi-opened semi-infinite waveguide in the two-dimensional case is investigated

articleTitle: On Inner Electrodynamic Problem in Domains with Fractal Boundaries
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In the present work, we apply the concept of fractional calculus to basic inner electrodynamic problem. The fractal approach is applied to the analysis of surface impedance which arises on the surface of simulated metamaterial environment plate in rectangular waveguide. The phenomenon testifies to possibility control of wave's propagation in waveguides partly filled by simulated medium

articleTitle: Frequency-plane branch-point singularities in the analysis of modal interactions on guided-wave structures
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Complex frequency-plane branch-point singularities are investigated in connection with mode interaction phenomena on guided-wave structures. It is found that certain types of branch points are directly associated with the leaky-wave cutoff behavior and modal interaction regimes on planar dielectric slab waveguides (including nonreciprocal waveguides) and printed-circuit transmission lines. The evolution of branch points in the complex frequency plane controls the modal behavior in the regions of interest. An important conclusion is that, in general, the discrete mode spectrum of guided-wave structures is not unique

articleTitle: Mixed potential integral equation for planar structures with ferrite layers
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Planar circuits including arbitrarily magnetized ferrite layers are analyzed in this presentation. The mixed-potential integral equation (MPIE) in the space domain is used to achieve that goal. First, a method to numerically generate the appropriate Green's functions from spectral domain counterparts is reported. These Green's functions are then used in the frame of a MPIE scheme. Special details concerning the treatment of singular integrals appearing in the computation of the entries of the method of moments matrix are considered. The final result is a method to solve planar structures with ferrite layers that, when compared with previous spectral domain implementations, combines the numerical advantages of working with potentials as well as the flexibility for analyzing non-rectangular shape conductors

articleTitle: Kinetics of Pulsed Electromagnetic Generators Based on Superfluorescence with Taking Into Account Medium and Cavity
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Basic kinetic equation and kinetic equation for the total quasispin of an emitter subsystem have been obtained for the Dicke Hamiltonian modified with terms describing the motion of emitters in the framework of the reduced description method. A way to estimation of loss influence is outlined

articleTitle: Surface Josephson Plasma Waves in Layered HTC Superconductors and their Excitation via Attenuated Total Reflection
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The detailed theoretical analysis of the resonance phenomena caused by excitation of the surface Josephson plasma waves (SJPW) in layered superconductors is made. It is shown that the surface waves at the boundary between the vacuum and layered superconductor can be excited by attenuated total reflection (ATR). The dispersion relation for the SJPW and the intensity of the reflected wave are investigated. The parameters of the problem (optimal thickness of vacuum layer, optimal wavelength) corresponding to the total suppression of specular reflection (TSSR) are found

articleTitle: Excitation of Nonstationary Electromagnetic Waves by an Electron Bunch that Intersects a Two-Dimensional Electron Gas
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Transition radiation of nonharmonic nonstationary pulses by an electron bunch that crosses a two-dimensional electron gas at the interface of two plasma media has been investigated. The Poynting vector of the lowest nonstationary harmonic is calculated. It has been shown that the information about properties of a two-dimensional electron gas can be obtained by the analysis of the leading front of the resulting signal

articleTitle: Modeling Reliability Characteristics of Compound Electromagnetic Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A method of investigation of reliability parameters of compound systems by means of generating functions is developed taking account of aging of the system's output elements. Main reliability characteristics of compound electromagnetic systems are examined in this paper. Expressions for the failure probability, the failure frequency and the failure rate are worked out in the cases when the lifetime of ageing output elements is circumscribed by the Weibull distribution

articleTitle: Nonlinear dynamics of globally coupled oscillators: exact solutions
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In the present paper we study analytically the nonlinear dynamics of globally coupled oscillators in the framework of order parameters approach. The main result is the exact analytical solution of the nonlinear system describing the behavior of the oscillators in the orthogonal reduction. We have obtained complete description of all possible phase portraits, the exact expressions for the attracting manifolds including the limit cycle and have derived analytical solutions for arbitrary initial data

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Waves Radiation from Periodic Boundary Dispersive of Dispersive Dielectric
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The transformation of inhomogeneous waves in the dispersive metamaterial into the radiating harmonics on its periodic boundary is considered. It is shown, that due to the dispersion of the material the additional resonances in the radiation pattern appear and this gives a new possibility for surface waves antennas design

articleTitle: On Resonance Diffraction of High Frequency Radiation at Periodically Corrugated Semiconductor Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We show that resonance features analogous to the well known in optics Wood-type anomalies can be observed at THz range on a periodically profiled surface of a high doped semiconductor at low temperatures. The anomalies are caused by surface plasmon polariton excitation at diffraction on the surface. The results are of interest both from physical viewpoint and in view of wide field of possible applications in nowadays information technologies

articleTitle: The Influence of Coulomb Interaction on Spatial Resolution of Charged Particles Nanobeams in Modern Projetion and Scanning Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The influence of space charge effect and effects of stochastic Coulomb interaction on spatial resolution of charged particles beams is theoretically studied. The beams of nonrelativistic protons and electrons with a radius about 1 nm were investigated. The cases of different energies in the range of currents from pA to muA typical for modern facilities were examined. Beam broadening due to influence of a space charge with the set distribution and also due to influence of stochastic effects of pair Coulomb interactions was studied. The regions of particles energies and beam currents under which effects of space charge and stochastic interaction of the charged particles have significant influence on spatial resolution are selected

articleTitle: An Optimized Quasi-Point Matching Fictitious Sources Method: Application to Scattering by a Buried Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A quasi-point matching method with fictitious sources (QPM-FS) is introduced and clarified by investigating the electromagnetic scattering problem by a cylinder, buried in a two-layered earth medium. This method reduces the effects of several numerical instabilities of the standard method of auxiliary sources (MAS) and thus is expected to treat more efficiently electrically large or complex problems

articleTitle: Waveguide Antenna Synthesis in the Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The synthesis problem for the waveguide antennas according to the prescribed amplitude radiation characteristics in the wide range of frequencies is considered. At the same time, the series of various requirements to the amplitude radiation pattern and front-to-rear factor in the operating frequency range as well as outside of this range can be taken into account when formulating the variational problem. The methods of successive approximations are used for solving the received nonlinear integral equations; the direct optimization of initial functional by the gradient methods is used too. The results of numerical modeling are presented

articleTitle: Implicit Function Method in Nonlinear Spectral Problems, Arising in the Antennas Synthesis Theory
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The two-dimensional nonlinear spectral problem on eigenvalues is reduced to investigation and numerical solution of the Cauchy problem for the first order linear differential equation by implicit function method

articleTitle: Using of the Schwartz method for solving a problem of diffraction on a periodic structure
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The building of general algorithm of solving the diffraction problem by the Schwartz method is considered. A diffraction problem associated with a linear waveguide phased antenna array is analyzed

articleTitle: Homogenization of Maxwell's Equations
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We consider the electromagnetic field in the domain with a perfectly conducting grid made of thin intersecting wires. The grid is supposed to be dependent on a small parameter epsiv>0 such that when epsivrarr0 the diameters of the wires tend to zero, the density of the grid increases and the grid is located in an arbitrary small neighborhood of a smooth surface Gamma. We study the asymptotic behavior of the solutions of Maxwell's equations when epsiv rarr 0

articleTitle: Forming and Transportation of an Electron Bunch in the Undulator
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Theoretical and experimental investigations of conditions of electron beam forming in axisymmetric focusing system are presented in this paper. Conditions of an electron bunch excitation in an undulator, consisting of ring magnets placed periodically with alternative polarity along a drift channel axis, have been theoretically studied. The relation between bunch dimensions, number of electrons and bunch lifetime has been obtained by using the virial theorem. The undulator motion of nonrelativistic electron beam is experimentally shown in a system with axial symmetrical magnetic disks

articleTitle: NonBragg selective reflection of electromagnetic waves in the spatially periodic medium
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: For the selective reflection of electromagnetic waves in spatially periodic media the violation is considered to the Bragg's conditions. Poincare-Lindstadt method for construction of periodic solution of the differential equation with periodic coefficient as expansion in terms of a small parameter is used

articleTitle: Adequacy of Direction Finding by a Circular Antenna Array in the Presence of the Field Scattered from a PEC Cylinder of Finite Length Situated on the PEC plane
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Dual integral equations are used to solve the problem of diffraction by a cylinder with arbitrary ratio of radius to length. Axial and transverse currents are taken into account. Convergence of slowly convergent Fourier integrals in the matrix elements of obtained SLAE is improved. Efficiency and accuracy of the developed algorithm is confirmed by comparison with the results of theoretical and experimental works of the other authors. The results for the on-axis electric field in the near-field zone are used for the modeling of the direction finding procedure for a circular antenna array

articleTitle: Polarization and Scattering Characteristics of Light Waves Diffracted from Metal-On-Dielectric Double-Periodic Structures
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic field characteristics are calculated with the full-wave technique based on the integral equations of microscopic electrodynamics. Theoretical results are presented for the characteristics of the light waves diffracted from planar double-periodic metal structures placed on top of a dielectric half-space. The obtained results demonstrate the polarization state changes in light diffracted from chiral planar structures. Furthermore, light transmission through optically thick metal films perforated with a periodic array of subwavelength holes is studied

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Wave Scattering from a Subsurface Wirelines
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Asymptotic relations for calculating of EM fields, scattered by underground wirelines of communication in the case of various illumination direction and sounding signal polarization were obtained. The calculating formulae were obtained on the practically existing stipulation that the cable diameter is essentially smaller then the illumination wave-length and depth of cable location in a ground. Details of calculating algorithm and modeling results are discussed

articleTitle: Simulation and Design Verification for Fully Integrated Radio Frequency (RF) Transceivers. Problems and Solutions.
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: This paper deals with the problems of simulation and design verification for fully integrated radio frequency (RF) transceivers. Single package solutions and multiple radio systems integrated on the same substrate provide extremely limited access to the intermediate stages for testing, if any. It becomes exceedingly critical to verify the design prior to the manufacturing. Capabilities and limitations of various mathematical methods that can be applied in the circuit simulation and final pre-manufacturing verification are discussed. The hybrid frequency/time domain technique that is considered to be the most promising and accurate tool for the integrated RF design verification is presented

articleTitle: The Third Harmonic Generation in E-Plane Waveguide on an Inhomogeneous Film with Cubic Nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper we consider an E-plane waveguide loaded by transversally inhomogeneous nonlinear film. Effects of the third harmonic generation are theoretically investigated. System of nonlinear equations for amplitudes of space-time harmonics is obtained. Phenomenon of resonant increasing of amplitude of the third harmonic caused by combination of film nonlinearity and its transversal inhomogeneity is investigated. Strong hysteresis phenomena are observed when amplitude or frequency of incident wave changes

articleTitle: Wgm Resonator Illuminated by Temporally Switched Internal Source
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Theoretical investigation of whispering gallery mode, WGM, resonator excitation by temporally switched source is carried out. Study is performed in rigorous mathematical manner using Green's function approach. Analytical solution obtained in Laplace transform domain is inverted with simple numerical technique to yield a time domain representation. Attention is focused upon the spectrum of cavity resonances excited, in particular how the practically important WGMs are established over time, and the transient radiation fields

articleTitle: Propagation of Coherent Light Throught Optically Inhomogeneous Media
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Phenomenon of a depolarization for optical signals which were propagated in media with the statistically distributed parameters has been investigated theoretically and has been confirmed experimentally. Polarization characteristics were calculated by using a coherent matrix method. The dependence of polarization degree of wave on parameters of scattering medium has been calculated for the Fraunhofer diffraction zone

articleTitle: Inverse Problem Solution for Multilayered Waveguide and Coaxial Structures
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The results of full-wave analysis of open and shielded rectangular waveguide and coaxial probes for multilayered substrate structures and its inverse problem solutions for measurement of substrate parameters have been obtained and presented. They have been used for control, test and measurement of substrate parameters, including the implementation of noninvasive methods

articleTitle: Numerical Gradient Integral-Equation Technique in 2-D Shaped Reflector Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: An accurate near-field diffraction synthesis method for 2-D shaped reflectors in the E-polarized wave is presented. The implemented method is based on a singular integral equation (SIE), which is descretized with the method of discrete singularities (MDS). The gradient of the objective function is derived with the aid of a certain SIE whose right-hand part is computed from the electric field SIE for the surface current. Such a semi-analytical gradient method is favorably timesaving and has controlled accuracy of computations

articleTitle: Transient response of circular waveguide modes on refractive index change in core
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We present an analytical solution of a problem of a circular waveguide mode transformation due to time refractive index change in a core. The scenario is that a natural mode propagates in the waveguide at the moment when the refractive index changes abruptly in time along all length of the waveguide. Ideal dielectric waveguide and waveguide with perfectly conducting wall are considered. The comparative analysis is performed

articleTitle: Near-Field Electromagnetic Tomography
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A new method of the electromagnetic tomography that uses data of the 2-dimensional (2D) scanning of an inhomogeneous half-space along its plane interface has been worked out. Signal parameters should be measured in dependence on a parameter of the received signal that determines the effective depth of its formation. This method is based on the solution of 3D integral equation. The application of this method to the passive and active microwave sounding has been considered, as well as the possibility of its application in the scanning near-field optical microscopy.

articleTitle: The hypersingular equation technique for the 3-D problem of diffraction on a metal screen in a stratified medium
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper, a problem of the electric type plane wave scattering on a flat screen is considered. The specific difficulty of the problem is associated with a non-homogeneous nature of the surrounding medium. A hypersingular integral equation (HSIE) was constructed by using the parameterized integral representation method. The numerical scheme for the scattered field evaluation was implemented based on the discrete frames method. Sample numerical results are presented

articleTitle: Axialy-Symmetric Excitation of a Fabry-Perot Rezonator Made of Two PEC Disks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We consider the diffraction of a given axially–symmetric electromagnetic wave by two zero-thickness stacked PEC disks. We derive a set of dual coupled integral equations in terms of scalar Hankel transforms that enable us to perform analytical regularization with the aid of the static part inversion.

articleTitle: Rapid Calculation of 3D Rectangular Waveguide Discontinuities
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A technique that allows one to increase the efficiency of 3D rectangular waveguide discontinues calculation is presented. The algorithm is based on the decomposition of 3D problem into a set of subproblems that can be solved using only the scalar bases. This approach is able to speed up the calculation of the S-matrix of the structure under consideration in 2-10 times depending on the complexity of the original device

articleTitle: Scattering of Reflector Antenna with Conic Dielectric Radome
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The calculation method for radar cross-section (RCS) of reflector antenna placed under cone-shape dielectric radome has been proposed. The method based on the integral equations for desired scattering field obtained with using Lorenz lemma. These integral equations considered electromagnetic interaction between antenna dish and radome. The analysis of RCS calculation results for model antenna system with conic dielectric radome has been carried out

articleTitle: Mode Transformers Based on the Waved Bends of Waveguides of Complicated Cross-Section
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The algorithm for calculation and optimization of mode transformers based on the curved rectangular waveguides with metal ridges is developed. The eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the waveguide are calculated using the mode matching technique with the account of the field singularities at the edges. The calculation of amplitude coefficients of propagating modes in irregular waveguides is accomplished by the cross-section method

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave diffraction on a resistive cone with longitudinal slots
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A problem of exciting a resistive cone with longitudinal periodical slots by a magnetic radial dipole is considered. Resistive sheet boundary conditions are used for simulating inhomogeneous curve linear surface properties (cone curvature is taken into account). The solution method is based on applying the Kontorovich-Lebedev integral transforms and a semi-inversion method. Special impedance effects are studied by analyzing analytical solutions
